data.gender_notes: Nereida is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Nereids are sea nymphs, daughters of the sea god Nereus and the sea nymph Doris. They are associated with water, fertility, and the sea. The name Nereida carries the meaning “Sea nymph” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Nereida usually hope their child will grow to embody sea nymph and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_english.name: Nereida
in_english.long_meaning: The name Nereida originates from Greek mythology, specifically from the Nereids, the daughters of Nereus, a sea god. The Nereids were known for their stunning beauty and were often depicted as sea nymphs or mermaids. In Christian tradition, the name Nereida symbolizes beauty, elegance, and a connection to the sea and its spiritual significance.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Nereida, a Christian name derived from Greek mythology, symbolizes the grace and beauty of the sea nymph Nereid. It represents a deep connection to the natural world, the fluidity of emotions, and the calming influence of the ocean. In spiritual terms, Nereida signifies a gentle, caring, and nurturing soul who embodies the divine feminine.

historical_references.reference: According to mythology, Nereida was a sea nymph, one of the fifty beautiful daughters of the Old Greek God Nereus and the Oceanid Doris. Nereus was a shape-shifter and his daughters were known as the Nereids. They were believed to protect sailors and fishermen, and were often represented as beautiful women with flowing hair and the upper bodies of fish.

Another reference to Nereida comes from the Christian tradition. In this context, Nereida is the name of a martyr, venerated as a saint, who lived in the 3rd century in Spain. She is said to have been a maiden of noble birth, who, when threatened with forced marriage to a pagan, chose to embrace Christianity and was put to death for her faith.
